result.summary: This Outsourcing Agreement governs the licensing of E.piphany applications and professional services to High Speed Net Solutions, Inc. (HSNS). The contract heavily favors the vendor, featuring strict customer indemnification obligations, forfeiture of prepaid fees upon termination, and vendor ownership of custom deliverables. HSNS faces significant operational and financial exposure under the current terms.

categoryScores.comment: R-INDEM-01 Fail: The contract requires the Customer to indemnify the Vendor for outsourcing services and IP infringement claims without providing reciprocal protections.
R-LIAB-01 Fail: Vendor liability is capped at total payments under the initial term, and mutual waiver of consequential damages heavily restricts recovery.
R-TERM-01 Fail: The agreement lacks a termination for convenience right for the Customer, only allowing termination for cause or insolvency.
R-IP-01 Fail: Vendor retains ownership of all deliverables and custom modifications created under the agreement, contrary to customer work product ownership rules.
R-PRIV-01 Not Addressed: The contract is completely silent on data security breach notification timelines and compliance standards.
R-PAY-01 Partial: Deliverables are deemed automatically accepted within 10 days if no list of material non-conformities is provided, though payment terms are milestone-based.

keyFacts.label: Liability Cap
keyFacts.value: Sum total of payments made under initial term

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Represents the vendor's interests to maximize protection and revenue retention.
agentPerspectives.stance: Firm on retaining IP ownership and limiting liability while securing broad customer indemnification.
keyPoints: Vendor retains all right, title, and interest in deliverables and customizations.
Customer indemnifies vendor against outsourcing service claims and third-party IP infringement.
All payments made by customer are strictly non-refundable upon termination.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Resist customer requests for mutual IP ownership and maintain the total initial term payments cap.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Focuses on closing the transaction while mitigating catastrophic deal risks.
agentPerspectives.stance: Pragmatic compromise needed on acceptance periods and termination rights to move forward.
keyPoints: Development fees are substantial at $230,500 with structured milestone payments.
Automatic acceptance after 10 days creates delivery pressure for the customer.
Post-termination usage rights are limited to 12 months for existing outsourcing customers.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Offer a slightly extended review period for deliverables in exchange for firm payment commitments.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Evaluates contract against enterprise buyer playbook standards and risk tolerances.
agentPerspectives.stance: High exposure identified due to severe indemnification imbalances and lack of data breach terms.
keyPoints: Fails R-INDEM-01 due to unmitigated customer indemnification of vendor.
Fails R-IP-01 because vendor owns all custom deliverables and modifications.
Fails R-TERM-01 as there is no termination for convenience clause for the customer.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Mandate the inclusion of mutual indemnification, customer work product ownership, and a 30-day termination for convenience right.

redlines.originalText: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners (each, an "Indemnified Party") against any and all claims
redlines.proposedText: Each party shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other party from and against third-party claims arising from its gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of this Agreement, and E.piphany shall indemnify HSNS for third-party intellectual property infringement.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will argue that standard terms require users of the application to bear the risks associated with providing outsourcing services to third parties.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Unilateral indemnification exposes HSNS to limitless financial liability for third-party claims without reciprocal protection for vendor IP risks.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: A balanced, mutual indemnification structure combined with robust vendor IP indemnification protects the customer from infringement claims.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can accept mutual indemnification for third-party claims, provided E.piphany stands behind its software's non-infringement.

redlines.originalText: IN NO EVENT SHALL E.PIPHANY'S LIABILITY HEREUNDER EXCEED THE SUM TOTAL OF PAYMENTS MADE BY HSNS UNDER THE INITIAL TERM OF THIS AGREEMENT.
redlines.proposedText: Each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall be capped at the fees paid or payable by HSNS in the preceding twelve (12) months, excluding breaches of confidentiality or IP indemnification.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will insist that the liability cap reflects the total economic value of the contract and matches their risk exposure.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: A liability cap tied to total initial term payments without carve-outs creates an unbalanced risk profile.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Aligning the liability cap to a standard 12-month trailing fee structure with customary exclusions ensures parity and protects against runaway damages.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can structure the cap around twelve months of fees, provided confidentiality and IP breaches remain uncapped.

redlines.originalText: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and may be renewed for successive one (1) year terms pursuant to mutual written agreement
redlines.proposedText: This Agreement shall continue for an initial term and may be terminated by Customer for convenience upon thirty (30) days prior written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will argue that fixed terms are necessary to amortize their development licensing costs and ensure revenue predictability.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Lacking a termination for convenience traps HSNS in a multi-year commitment if the software fails to meet business needs.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Incorporating a 30-day termination for convenience right aligns with enterprise buyer standards for vendor performance management.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We require a 30-day convenience exit to maintain operational flexibility, but we can agree to amortize upfront development fees upon early exit.

redlines.originalText: HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to any customization, enhancement, amendment or changes made by or for HSNS pursuant to this Agreement
redlines.proposedText: HSNS shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to all custom deliverables and work product created specifically for HSNS, granting E.piphany a license solely to provide the services.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will maintain that enhancements to their proprietary application must remain their intellectual property to protect their core software integrity.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Assigning all custom modifications strips HSNS of ownership in proprietary workflows developed for its business.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Customer ownership of custom work product protects proprietary business processes while allowing the vendor to retain background IP.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can grant E.piphany ownership of core platform improvements while retaining ownership of custom workflows specific to our operations.

obligations.breachConsequence: Legal liability and breach of contract

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Indemnification — Market Mutual IP & Third-Party Indemnification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer... Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Provider...
deviations: Indemnification appears one-sided towards protecting E.piphany rather than fully mutual.
missingProtections: Explicit IP infringement indemnification from Provider to Customer.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Revise indemnification to ensure mutual protections for intellectual property infringement claims.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: 3.1, 3.4, 4.3, 6.2, 6.4, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Provisions which by their nature should survive termination, including confidentiality, indemnification, limitation of liability, payment of accrued fees, data return and deletion, and governing law, survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement.
deviations: Survival relies on an enumerated list of section numbers rather than descriptive categories.
missingProtections: Explicit catch-all for provisions that by their nature should survive.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure the enumerated list of surviving sections is exhaustive and up to date.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: THIS ALLOCATION TO WHICH THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED. THIS LIMITATION OF LIABILITY APPLIES NOTWITHSTANDING ANY FAILURE OF THE ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF THE EXCLUSIVE REMEDIES.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Limitation of Liability — 12-Month Trailing Aggregate Fee Cap with Balanced Super-Cap
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Consequential Damages Waiver... (b) General Aggregate Cap... (c) Super-Cap for Data Protection Breaches...
deviations: The excerpt primarily highlights the failure of essential purpose and termination rather than a clear fee cap formula.
missingProtections: Explicit 12-month trailing aggregate fee cap and super-cap definitions.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Incorporate a clear aggregate liability cap based on trailing fees.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS acknowledges that E.piphany retains all right, title and interest in the Application and any modifications thereto...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Rights — Customer Work Product Ownership & Non-Use of Customer Data for AI Training
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data. Provider shall not use Customer Data... to train, fine-tune... any generalized artificial intelligence...
deviations: Modifications and customizations are assigned to E.piphany rather than ensuring Customer work product ownership.
missingProtections: Restrictions on using customer data for AI model training.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Add explicit language protecting customer data from being used for AI training.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: For any breach of the warranties contained in Section 4.1, HSNS's sole and exclusive remedy, and E.piphany's entire liability, shall be: (i) to correct the nonconforming Application...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Warranties — Performance Warranty with Re-Performance Remedy
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: The Provider warrants that... If a warranty is breached and reported within ninety (90) days, the Provider shall re-perform or correct the non-conformity...
deviations: Remedies focus heavily on correction or license termination rather than standardized re-performance windows.
missingProtections: Clear 90-day reporting window with explicit re-performance obligations for services.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Align warranty remedies with standard re-performance and refund timelines.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to any customization, enhancement, amendment or changes made by or for HSNS pursuant to this Agreement...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Ownership — Each Party Keeps Its Pre-Existing IP; Licence to Deliverables
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Each party retains all rights in its intellectual property existing before or developed independently of this Agreement. The Customer owns all deliverables created specifically for it upon payment.
deviations: Customizations are assigned to E.piphany rather than Customer owning deliverables created specifically for it.
missingProtections: Clear retention of pre-existing IP by both parties.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Clarify pre-existing IP ownership and ensure custom deliverables vest with the client.

rules.evidence: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany
rules.explanation: The contract requires the Customer to indemnify the Vendor for outsourcing services and IP infringement claims without providing reciprocal protections.
rules.recommendation: Revise Section 10.2 to make indemnification mutual and remove customer obligations to indemnify vendor for third-party IP infringement.

rules.evidence: IN NO EVENT SHALL E.PIPHANY'S LIABILITY HEREUNDER EXCEED THE SUM TOTAL OF PAYMENTS MADE BY HSNS UNDER THE INITIAL TERM OF THIS AGREEMENT.
rules.explanation: Vendor liability is capped at total payments under the initial term, and mutual waiver of consequential damages heavily restricts recovery.
rules.recommendation: Amend Section 11 to set a standard 12-month fees cap with customary carve-outs for IP infringement, data breaches, and confidentiality.

rules.evidence: Upon prior written notice, either party may terminate this Agreement if the other party becomes insolvent... or fails to cure a material breach
rules.explanation: The agreement lacks a termination for convenience right for the Customer, only allowing termination for cause or insolvency.
rules.recommendation: Add a provision allowing Customer to terminate for convenience with 30 days written notice and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

rules.evidence: HSNS acknowledges and agrees that any and all Deliverables shall be and remain the property of E.piphany.
rules.explanation: Vendor retains ownership of all deliverables and custom modifications created under the agreement, contrary to customer work product ownership rules.
rules.recommendation: Modify Section 6.4 and Section 13 to state that custom deliverables and work product developed for Customer are owned by Customer.

rules.explanation: The contract is completely silent on data security breach notification timelines and compliance standards.
rules.recommendation: Insert a data privacy clause requiring Vendor to notify Customer of any security breach within 24 to 48 hours.

rules.evidence: Each Deliverable shall be deemed accepted upon the earlier of: (i) receipt of written notice of acceptance... or (ii) ten (10) days after delivery
rules.explanation: Deliverables are deemed automatically accepted within 10 days if no list of material non-conformities is provided, though payment terms are milestone-based.
rules.recommendation: Extend the deemed acceptance period to at least 30 days and ensure payment terms explicitly specify Net 45 upon verified milestone signoff.
